one_line: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit triggers market, policy, and supply-chain fallout as AI funding and regulation advance.

themes.title: Nvidia leadership shakeup rattles markets
themes.text: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO following an investigation into personal relationships, with CFO Colette Kress named interim chief. Shares fell 4.34% while AMD rose 5.86%, and investors, Elon Musk, and analysts raised questions about succession, open-source AI strategy, and supply-chain deals.

themes.title: U.S. probes Nvidia chip sales to China
themes.text: Congressional Democrats launched an inquiry into the Trump administration's handling of Nvidia chip sales to China and export licenses, following the CEO's ouster amid a scandal linking company leadership, government officials, and foreign shipments. The probe follows reports that Southeast Asian data centers exploited a sanctions gap to route Nvidia chips to Chinese companies.

themes.title: AI infrastructure funding accelerates
themes.text: Databento raised a $100M Series C at a $1.1B valuation, Nebuly raised $21M to measure AI agent ROI, Nidus raised $30M for AI robotics in defense factories, and TSMC announced a $500M fund for chip startups and suppliers.

themes.title: Regulators and researchers weigh AI oversight
themes.text: Ethan Mollick reported 63% of 173 AI benchmarks cited by labs since 2023 are now saturated, and SEBI announced upcoming AI usage guidelines for capital markets emphasizing human-in-the-loop. India's MeitY also opened a consent manager registration portal under the DPDP Act.
